humanities_role_explanation: Historical Czech documents (OCR'd books and periodicals) supply the texts, but the competence tested is generic topic localization (span-level text understanding), not a disciplinary humanities skill.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: OCR output (PERO-OCR) from scanned historical Czech pages, split into 768-1024 character segments; topics given as name plus short description.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Topic localization: identifying word-level spans expressing a given topic (name + description), with overlapping and non-contiguous spans; also text-level topic presence detection (document-level zero-shot classification). Span labeling via tagging and matching paradigms.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task, topic localization, on Czech historical texts.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-5.2, GPT-5-mini, GPT-5-nano, gpt-oss-20b, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 3.2 3B, Gemma 3 27B/4B, Gemini 3 Pro Preview; plus fine-tuned BERT-style encoders.

quantitative_metrics.note: Precision, recall, F1, IoU, localization success at IoU thresholds, Krippendorff's alpha, bootstrap CIs.

summary: The paper introduces CzechTopic, a human-annotated benchmark for zero-shot topic localization in historical Czech documents, with topics defined by name and description and annotated word-level spans. Evaluation is relative to human pairwise agreement rather than a single gold annotation. LLMs and BERT cross-encoders distilled from gpt-5-mini annotations are benchmarked.
key_findings: Best LLM (gpt-5-2) reaches word-level F1 61.1 and IoU 48.7 versus human baseline 68.7 F1 and 57.2 IoU; text-level F1 80.6 vs 83.2. LLM word F1 ranges from 13.2 to 61.1. Best distilled BERT (robeczech) gets word F1 48.3. Matching beats tagging by 0.104 F1; few-shot adds 0.010; prompt language has no effect. Krippendorff's alpha 0.616 (micro).
dataset_size: 525 texts (363 topics, 1,820 annotated text-topic pairs) in the human-annotated benchmark; an additional distilled development set of 15,550 texts is separate.
evaluation_unit: topic (macro-averaged over topics; 1,820 annotated text-topic pairs across 525 texts)
facets_explanation: Human annotators defined topics (Phase 1) and localized spans independently (Phase 2) following written guidelines and regular meetings; their disciplinary training is not stated, so domain_expert is a weak reading. Evaluation is against all annotators' spans via average pairwise agreement rather than a single gold, so divergence is treated as informative; the paper tests that annotators agree more with each other than with the topic author. A separate development set was LLM-generated (gpt-5-mini) but is not the evaluation key.
results_explanation: Best LLM gpt-5-2-2025-12-11 has word-level F1 61.1 (human baseline 68.7), so gap is 8 points (68.7-61.1=7.6, rounded). Gap points 10 derive from ablation: matching improves word F1 by 0.104 over tagging (converted to ~10 points); few-shot vs zero-shot 0.010.
